newsitem.title: JAPAN: Colombian coffee exporters eye Asian market.
newsitem.headline: Colombian coffee exporters eye Asian market.

text.p: Colombia, one of the world's largest coffee producers, will try to boost exports to Asia, particularly South Korea and China, Colombian coffee industry officials said on Tuesday.
"The Asian market has a great potential for growth, and we're going to have strategic marketing here," said Richard Gutierrez, commercial counsellor at the Colombian embassy in Tokyo.

Gutierrez, who is also the Tokyo representative for the National Federation of Coffee Growers of Colombia, said the country has a strategic alliance with South Korea's Lotte business group to promote coffee consumption.
"Promoting canned coffee drinks is one of our targets," he said.
In Japan, the world's third-largest coffee consumer after the United States and Germany, Colombia already has a strong foothold, accounting for 22 percent of the 327,000 tonnes imported last year.
"Japan is surely the main target. but we're interested in other consumers in this region," said Steven Diaz, a director of Frederman Hincapie Parra, a Colombian coffee exporter.
In Taiwan as well, Colombia now has a strategic alliance with UCC Taiwan to boost coffee sales, the FNC's Gutierrez said.

"North America and Europe have been the traditional markets for us, but we're now going to sell more coffee to Asia," said Felipe Isaza, general manager of Exportadora De Cafe Condor, one of Colombia's major coffee exporters.

Isaza said Asian coffee consumption is rising by six percent per year, while bean demand in Europe is almost stagnant. He said that South Korea, Taiwan, Singapore and Hong Kong will be the main targets.
Colombian industry officials said that promoting coffee sales in China has been harder than they originally expected, citing its traditional tea culture.
"We're starting coffee sales slowly in China. But tea is very strong there, and it's difficult and time-consuming to change their culture," Isaza said.
But the FNC's Gutierrez said they opened Colombian coffee shops in Shanghai and Beijing in an attempt to boost their profile among Chinese consumers.
The Colombian coffee officials are in Japan to attend an international food exhibition being held in Chiba Prefecture, east of Tokyo, this week.
